analysis.title: Asia Thematic Strategy: Why AI remains foremost
key_insights: Asia price action in 2026 is AI vs non-AI, with little differentiation among other sectors or markets. JPM expects the pattern to continue in 2027, and AI stock performance will drive both allocation alpha and overall market beta.

AI stocks are now more than 50% of MSCI Asia ex-Japan weight and are expected to contribute about 70% of AxJ earnings growth in 2027, similar to 2026. Korea and Taiwan together are close to 50% of MSCI EM.

Asian AI exposure is mainly hardware (Taiwan, Korea, some China). The hardware layer has pricing power because demand exceeds supply, which JPM expects through at least 2028. Ecosystem net income is projected to exceed $1tn by 2028 and free cash flow to reach about $700bn.

The hardware trade moved from volume to pricing/margin late last year. The key question is now how long the spending cycle lasts, which depends on how well AI is monetized at the hyperscalers and, more importantly, at the model and application layer.
JPM says investors persistently underprice the length of the cycle. Current memory-sector valuations price in very bearish end-of-cycle conditions.

The most persistent shortages are expected in advanced logic and packaging, semiconductor equipment, ABF substrates, high-end CCL materials, HBM and high-speed optics. Commodity NAND is the clearest area where supply and demand may normalize earlier, though that could be delayed if memory makers keep shifting capacity to HBM.
Gross margin estimates across a broad sample of AI hardware companies have risen about 8% on average since Sep-25.

Hardware earnings are now macro-relevant in Korea and Taiwan. In Korea, aggregate market earnings over 2026-28 are 80% of GDP above the 2025 baseline, and the market-cap increase for local investors adds about 50% of GDP.

Hyperscaler economics are favorable. At current rental rates and five-year depreciation, a B200 datacenter earns about 30% ROI on conservative assumptions. Hyperscaler capex has shown little sensitivity to interest rates.

Hyperscalers are running out of self-funding because cash outflows come at build time and inflows come later. For now there is enough cash in the hardware layer, and credit access is stable. JPM expects the AI-only free cash flow hole to start closing by 2028 as capex growth slows from over 100% in 2026 to under 50% in 2027.
JPM's capex assumptions are $1tn, $1.4tn and $1.55tn for 2026-28. In 2027, AI capex growth is about 50%, real AI GW growth about 25%, and installed GW capacity growth about 60%.

The real hyperscaler constraints are procurement, politics/permitting and power, not funding. Power is increasingly supplied behind the meter. Cloud-like margins of about 30% are feasible for hyperscalers and software-like margins are not.

Model-layer pricing shifted to per-token in late 1Q 2026 and token subsidies faded. Enterprises hit token budgets this summer and moved demand to cheaper models, so aggregate token prices have deflated rapidly since mid-year. JPM says this may be a one-off adjustment.

Token volume is the most important model-layer variable. Agentic use and cybersecurity are the most imminent new use cases, and the report sets cybersecurity at an incremental $430bn+ 3-year TAM. Tokens are growing 10-20x annually while datacenter capacity grows 50-70% at most.

JPM's modest 2027 scenario has token prices deflating 70%, token consumption growing 10x, and AI ARR tripling to almost $1tn. With ~50% inference gross margins and inference at ~60% of compute, the model layer's operating profit run rate would be about $167bn. This implies hyperscaler ARR of about $833bn at end-2027.
AI ARR is on course to triple to over $300bn by end-2026. If ARR simply doubles every year, it will likely exceed annual capex by 2029.

Key risks are a material slowdown in token consumption growth, commoditization of models and hardware, power constraints, regulation and safety, and a failure of a large, interlinked AI company that cascades across the ecosystem. The 1999-2000 parallel (internet stocks peaked before picks-and-shovels) was more ominous in July-Aug but remains a risk.
Positioning is hard to read. Long-only investors often cannot be as overweight as they would like, and hedge fund positioning in AxJ Tech is substantially lighter than at the June highs.

Longer-term questions are economic displacement (AI revenue reaching single-digit % of GDP in two years), value capture that may spread more evenly across layers than in prior eras, K-shaped economy and wealth concentration, regulation and AI safety, and US-China geopolitics. JPM says current evidence is not enough to conclude on these.
JPM stays overweight Tech, Taiwan and Korea in regional allocation, and AI remains the biggest of its preferred themes.

sector_views.rationale: AI hardware has pricing power, supply tightness through at least 2028, and ecosystem net income above $1tn by 2028.
Macro conditions for non-AI sectors stay challenging with elevated rates and a widening K-shaped economy, and the sectors show little differentiation.

earnings_insights: JPM expects AI stocks to drive about 70% of AxJ earnings growth in 2027, similar to 2026 (consensus-based net income estimates).
Asian AI ecosystem net income is forecast to exceed $1tn by 2028 and free cash flow about $700bn (actuals and consensus estimates).
In Korea, consensus aggregate market earnings over 2026-28 are 80% of GDP above the 2025 baseline.

macro_indicators.interpretation: JPM Cloud Capex Database. Growth slows from over 100% in 2026 to under 50% in 2027, which should let AI free cash flow start improving by 2028.

macro_indicators.reading: over $300bn by year-end, more than 3x end-2025
macro_indicators.interpretation: About 0.25% of global GDP. It supports the case that the model layer can monetize.
Assumes token prices fall 70% and token consumption grows 10x.

macro_indicators.reading: $3 to $1 per million tokens (-66%) over the past year
macro_indicators.interpretation: Usage-weighted deflation pressures model-maker economics, but JPM says it may be a one-off adjustment.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight Tech, Taiwan and Korea in the regional allocation, with AI as the largest preferred theme
trade_ideas.rationale: AI hardware pricing power and supply tightness through at least 2028 drive earnings growth.
trade_ideas.risk: A material slowdown in token consumption growth.

risk_factors: A material slowdown in token consumption growth is the most important risk.
Commoditization of AI models and hardware as more supply comes online.
Power generation constraints on datacenter buildout.
Regulation and AI-safety shifts in the competitive landscape.
Segment-specific shifts in supply-demand balance and pricing power.
Concentration and interlinked financing mean a failure of a large AI company could cascade across the ecosystem.
Internet stocks in 1999-2000 peaked well before the downstream picks-and-shovels.
Valuations and positioning are hard to interpret.
vol_and_positioning: Hedge fund positioning in AxJ Tech is substantially lighter than at the June highs.
Long-only investors often cannot be as overweight AI as they would like.
AI positioning gets crowded periodically, as in the July pullback, but JPM says fundamentals should overcome such volatility.
Traditional valuation metrics fail in current conditions, so valuations and positioning are hard to interpret.
geopolitical: US-China competition in AI ecosystems, including how it could affect deployment timing, model-release cadence and semiconductor demand.
Possible regulatory change if open-source models or models from adversarial nations are deemed unsafe on security grounds.
Datacenter moratoriums and political movements to slow AI development (not yet a hot-button issue).

tension_points.bull_case: Hyperscaler ROI is above 30%, AI ARR is heading above $300bn, and a modest 2027 scenario (10x tokens, -70% price) gets ARR to almost $1tn and model-layer operating profit to about $167bn. Hardware supply tightness lasts through at least 2028.
tension_points.bear_case: Aggregate token prices have deflated rapidly since mid-year, AI firms lack platform-style moats, commoditization is a risk, and interlinked financing could cascade if a large company fails. Internet stocks peaked before picks-and-shovels in 1999-2000.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A material slowdown in token consumption growth. JPM says anything better than 2x annual ARR growth from the end-2026 level should be good enough.

theme_stances.key_argument: Supply-demand tightness gives Asian hardware firms pricing power through at least 2028, and the market underprices how long the cycle lasts.
theme_stances.evidence: markets have (naturally) persistently underpriced this longevity

theme_stances.key_argument: Per-token pricing and strong token volume give the model layer sufficient pathways to monetize.
theme_stances.evidence: there are sufficient pathways for the model layer to deliver on monetization
